common.eligibleRequests: All scheduled authorized in-quota requests for an advertised supported operation, including every retry, transport timeout, real test request and fixed-rate synthetic request. Correct intended negative denials are measured separately. Latency starts at scheduled dispatch, not worker availability; missed dispatches are failures. A durable acknowledgement requires committed operation identity and replay-safe intent before any success response.
common.exclusions: Only malformed input, expected authentication/authorization/quota negatives and caller cancellation before acceptance, labelled in advance with counts. No release-attributable, provider, timeout, overload, readiness or missing-sample failure is excluded. Separately authorized destructive paths outside the declared continuity envelope are reported as a separate campaign, never deleted from customer SLO history.
common.passFormula: eligible_success / eligible_attempts >= 0.9995; every profile and each non-noisy tenant separately passes all latency, throughput, queue, CPU, memory, recovery and fairness limits; zero lost accepted operations, duplicate logical resources, corrupt data, incorrect charge, imbalance or unauthorized success; all negatives deny; no unresolved release-blocking alert; all abort/rollback/cleanup checks pass. During supported zero-downtime upgrade additionally require zero release-attributable failed eligible requests and zero unavailable readiness samples. Missing evidence fails.
common.percentileFormula: Nearest rank over eligible latencies of the named sample unit: sorted value at ceil(p*N), p=0.50,0.95,0.99; timeouts use elapsed deadline and count as failures. Report counts, error classes and distributions by operation and tenant without averaging percentiles. A percentile SLO claim requires the profile minimum sample count for that named population; smaller lifecycle-trial populations report raw durations and completion bounds, never a qualified p99. Throughput is successful named sample units divided by steady-state wall seconds; unique side effects and retries are separately counted.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants, 100 projects each, 100 resources per project; 60% GET, 20% bounded list or watch establishment, 20% durable mutations. Every list page contains at most 100 resources; 10% mutations replay an existing idempotency key. One additional noisy tenant offers 10 times a normal tenant rate. Read/list latency includes complete response; mutations use durable acknowledgement.
profiles.failureWorkload: Lose an API replica, PostgreSQL leader and one supported server separately; hold an outbox delivery for 120 seconds and restart; prove tenant fairness, audit, no missing or double operations.
profiles.sampleUnit: Eligible GET, bounded list/watch establishment and durable mutation requests in the stated mix; count every scheduled attempt and report operation-class and tenant counts separately.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants, at most 100 simultaneous logical resources; balanced cycles of 25% provision, 25% resize, 25% suspend/resume, 25% deprovision. Resource-dependent steps wait for actual completion; independent identities preserve the offered rate. Repeat each provider latency and 10% lost-response condition; only supported actions are eligible. Completion deadline includes provider wait; request latency ends at durable acknowledgement.
profiles.failureWorkload: Restart after provider side effect but before response; expire credentials, rate-limit provider for 120 seconds and restore it; reconcile identity before retry; reservations balance.
profiles.sampleUnit: Durable acknowledgements of the stated real provision/resize/suspend-resume/deprovision mix, with 10% idempotent retries recorded separately from unique accepted operations. End-to-end provisioning is bounded by the completion deadline, not an acknowledgement percentile.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants and 1000 resources; at least 1000000 1-KiB events: 80% original, 10% exact duplicate, 5% 24-hour-late original, 5% corrections. Close 100 invoices with 1000 lines each, replay stream and correct closed invoices. All event classes, invoice close and read latencies are reported separately.
profiles.failureWorkload: Stop an ingest/rating replica and fail over PostgreSQL during invoice close; restore and replay stream; exact decimal ledger, invoice identity and zero double charge.
profiles.sampleUnit: Usage-event durable acknowledgements only, across the fixed original/duplicate/late/correction mix. Invoice closes, reads, credits and restore are separately counted complete lifecycle trials; one million event samples never means one million invoice closes.

profiles.workload: 20 browser, 20 CLI and 20 agent actors across 10 tenants; 40% resource/list, 20% operation timeline, 20% cost view, 20% preview and confirm mutation. Browser latency ends at rendered authoritative state; CLI/agent at complete result or durable operation identity.
profiles.failureWorkload: Refresh/login/session revocation during API replica loss; retry interrupted mutation using same identity; forbidden direct calls remain denied.
profiles.sampleUnit: Rendered authoritative browser responses or completed CLI/agent responses and durable acknowledgements in the stated interface mix. Long resource provisioning is a separate lifecycle trial.

profiles.workload: 10 tenant networks, 20 endpoints; equal fixed-rate 1-KiB IPv4 and IPv6 echo transactions across nodes plus policy-denial traffic. Separately run at least three complete network/subnet/address/policy create-update-delete trials per supported method with common durable acknowledgement limits.
profiles.failureWorkload: Lose one supported node/controller; 10-minute management outage; preserve in-scope flows, isolation, no address leaks or duplicate allocation.
profiles.sampleUnit: One complete 1-KiB IPv4 or IPv6 echo transaction. Network control lifecycle uses separate real trials and common durable acknowledgement bounds.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants with one 1-GiB volume each; 4-KiB random I/O, 70% read and 30% write, fsync every acknowledged write; fixed content seed 20260907. Separately run attach/resize/snapshot/restore/delete and digest readback with common durable acknowledgement limits.
profiles.failureWorkload: Lose a supported storage or attachment node; reject stale/multi-attach; snapshot/restore to another allowed node and compare all committed data.
profiles.sampleUnit: One completed 4-KiB read or fsynced write. Attach, resize, snapshot and full restore use separate real lifecycle trials.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants, 100 signed 1-MiB OCI blobs and two approved 1-GiB VM images; 70% verified 1-MiB GET, 20% resumable upload chunks, 10% metadata. End-to-end image import and boot use the completion deadline; control mutations use common acknowledgement limits.
profiles.failureWorkload: Interrupt upload, lose cache/registry replica, revoke sharing and restore metadata/content; digest persists across tag changes and retained references survive GC.
profiles.sampleUnit: One verified 1-MiB GET/upload chunk or bounded metadata response in the stated mix. Full image imports, registry round trips and VM boots are separate real lifecycle trials.

profiles.workload: 10 Linux VMs across allowed nodes; guest workload writes and fsyncs 1-KiB numbered records and reads their digests at fixed rate. Separately run at least three complete trials per supported create/access/start/stop/resize/snapshot/restore/delete method; control uses common durable acknowledgement limits.
profiles.failureWorkload: Lose VM host and management plane separately; measure declared live or cold recovery within single-failure RTO, preserve committed digest and unique VM/charge identity.
profiles.sampleUnit: One guest 1-KiB fsynced write/readback response. VM create, access, resize, snapshot, restore and delete use separate real lifecycle trials.

profiles.workload: Two tenant clusters, three test workload replicas each; equal HTTP GET and durable 1-KiB write/readback requests through tenant service, 10 users. Separately exercise cluster lifecycle, scale and supported adjacent-version upgrade; control uses common acknowledgement limits.
profiles.failureWorkload: Lose tenant worker/control-plane member and provider management separately; keep declared workload continuity; rotate/revoke credentials and restore isolated workload data.
profiles.sampleUnit: One tenant-workload HTTP GET or durable 1-KiB write/readback response. Cluster create, scale, upgrade, access rotation, repair and restore use separate real lifecycle trials.

profiles.workload: 10 tenant buckets, 1000 versioned 1-MiB objects per bucket; 50% GET, 20% PUT, 20% bounded LIST, 10% DELETE; retention/denial negatives separate. Run same profile against local reference and remote backend; multipart and metadata mutations use common acknowledgement limits.
profiles.failureWorkload: Lose storage/gateway node, interrupt multipart completion and remote response; rotate/revoke credential; restore metadata plus versions with digest and retention checks.
profiles.sampleUnit: One complete 1-MiB GET/PUT, bounded LIST or DELETE in the stated mix. Full metadata/object restore and credential lifecycle use separate real trials.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants, each with 1-GiB representative volume, VM, Kubernetes or object data; statistical requests are 25% backup-policy create, 25% policy/schedule update, 25% status read, 25% policy delete in balanced reusable cycles. Separately run at least three complete backup, isolated restore and retention-aware copy-delete trials per declared data class, with unique copies and recovered bytes/ownership verification. Record copy/restore bytes per second separately; they are not policy-request throughput.
profiles.failureWorkload: Target outage for 120 seconds, partial upload and control restart; verify off-cell RPO/RTO and retention, fail closed on partial copies, cleanup without deleting original data.
profiles.sampleUnit: Durable backup policy/schedule create, update and delete acknowledgements, plus bounded policy/status reads. Full backup, isolated restore and retained-copy deletion are separate real lifecycle trials; policy throughput never represents copied or recovered data throughput.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants and 20 actors; equal SSH, Kubernetes and console methods where claimed; request/approve/use/revoke in fixed cycles, 60-second grants, at least 1000 access-response samples across claimed methods, with at least three complete lifecycle trials per method. Control acceptance uses common acknowledgement limits; first authorized access uses response thresholds.
profiles.failureWorkload: Lose issuer/control replica; rotate key, revoke and restore state; grants expire at original deadline, restoration never revives access, wrong-target/cross-tenant denial.
profiles.sampleUnit: One completed first authorized access or bounded access control response for each claimed SSH, Kubernetes or console method. Full approval, expiry, recovery and key-rotation journeys are separately counted real trials.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants, at most 1000 cases; 40% case create/update, 30% consent/status, 20% read/escalate, 10% resolve. Case acknowledgement uses common limits. Separately create at least three independent redacted 10-MiB bundles and complete access, routing failure and restore journeys; each bundle strictly below 300 seconds. Paid test offering uses non-financial data.
profiles.failureWorkload: Disconnect external routing for 120 seconds, restart and restore; one durable case, preserved SLA clocks, revoked consent and no restored support grant.
profiles.sampleUnit: One complete case/consent/read/escalate/resolve control response. Full redacted bundle creation, external routing recovery and restore are separately counted lifecycle trials.

profiles.workload: 10 tenants, at most 100 simultaneous real authorized external test resources; balanced lifecycle cycles through discover/adopt/provision/use/hold/resize/deprovision using two independent adapters. Every provision is paired with completed deprovision; the rate applies to acknowledgements, with resource-dependent steps waiting for actual completion. Run provider latency/ambiguity mix; preserve resource/operation/usage identity across adapter replacement.
profiles.failureWorkload: Rotate credentials, rate-limit and disconnect remote API for 120 seconds; restart after side effect and replace adapter; no duplicate resource, charge or orphan.
profiles.sampleUnit: Durable acknowledgement of the stated real external lifecycle mix. Unique external effects, retries, provider completion and adapter replacement are counted separately from request throughput.
